title: FAQ
text:
Our usual Peer Share, Open Tying and 101 events are not ticketed, you just need to DM us for the address. We ask for a suggested donation of £10 to cover the cost of renting the hall.
Donations can be made in cash on the day, via our bank account (DM or get details on the day) or anonymously via our Open Collective platform.
You can also see all of our income and outgoings and donate to any specific fundraising we are doing outside of the need to pay our rent on our OC platform.



We don’t check who has donated or how much and we never want anyone to have to choose between attending RiS and meeting their basic needs.
In general we expect a donation from anyone who is in stable employment, has secure housing and is able to cover their household bills each month with some money left over for leisure spending.
If you are able to pay for holidays, education as entertainment or own your own home please consider donating a higher amount to help support us to keep RiS financially accessible for anyone.
If you are able to put aside money in long term savings each month (ie not just saving for a specific purchase), have any investments or own a business or property that generates profit without your direct labour, or charge rent to anyone for a property you own it is expected that you contribute a higher amount than our recommended donation.



We start setting up the hall at 6.30pm and encourage everyone to help out if they are able. We try to start an opening circle by 6.50pm and it is recommended to attend these at least your first few times at RiS. If for some reason you aren’t able to make it on time for the opening circle please speak to a rainbow lanyarded volunteer so they can make sure you have the important safety and orientation information! I have a disability, can I still come?
We have welcomed attendees with a range of disabilities over the course of our running. Please let us know if there is anything in particular you might need that is not covered below.
We recognise that conflicting access needs are not uncommon and that we may not be able to make the space perfectly accessible for everybody but we wish to be as supportive and transparent as possible about what we can do.
Our venue is fully wheelchair accessible, there is a lift from the ground floor to our main hall on the first floor and there are two accessible toilets on the same level. The fire safety regulations of the building state that in case of a fire wheelchair users who are not able to escape via the stairs should remain in the building until the fire and rescue service arrives.
We are mad and neurodivergent positive in our space and welcome attendees who might display unexpected behaviour such as stimming and vocal tics.
There is a quiet room located near our main hall, though this is communal to all users of the building and cannot be guaranteed to be empty. This is not an appropriate space for tying.
Our lighting is usually moderate and we play background music at a low level at most of our events.
We meet in a gym hall and as such the noise levels, especially overlapping sounds, can get relatively high due to the acoustics but we do try to keep this to a minimum.
People who are hard of hearing or have auditory processing struggles may find it difficult to follow taught classes due to the acoustics of the room but we will do our best to work with you to mitigate this if you let us know you need that support.
We have a DNO air purifier running near the centre of the room during all our events as well as hypochlorous acid sanitiser available for hands and hard surfaces. Our full Infectious Illness Policy is available here attendees are expected to stay away if they are exhibiting any symptoms.
There are chairs with back support and without arms available in the hall if sitting on the floor is not accessible for you.
The communal kitchen space has chairs with back support and without arms as well as bench style seating.



You are welcome to come alone, if you are especially nervous please speak to one of our rainbow lanyarded volunteers who will do their best to introduce you to people and help you feel welcome.



Do not expect to tie with someone new to you the first time you attend RiS. We encourage everyone who attends RiS to practice self-tying whether you prefer to top or bottom for rope.
Our 101 sessions are designed to enable self-tying and we encourage everyone to participate in these as there is useful and transferrable information for both roles.
We have a Connections Board to facilitate getting to know people and finding those who share compatible rope interests but people often spend time self-tying and getting to know people their first few times at RiS.



You can! We’d prefer if you let us know in advance as you would be our first point of contact if any incidents occurred that needed to be dealt with after the event. We only ask that you share our Values and Code of Conduct with them before attending.



Absolutely! We have all the basic equipment available to lend. There is also a Connections Board to help you meet people with similar goals and interests so just bring yourself and some enthusiasm.
Open Tying events are probably the least accessible for absolute beginners as most attendees will most likely be focused on their own tying plans, but we’re a friendly bunch and you won’t be turned away.
Our Peer Share sessions have more opportunity to connect with community members to show you the ropes and a learning corner with various books available.
If you’re looking for a more structured learning experience we’d recommend starting out at one of our quarterly 101 sessions which you should be able to find in our event listings.



Probably! Our community is varied and have many skills between us. This is primarily a peer sharing event and you will have to proactively seek out people who are able and willing to teach the skills you want to learn. We have a Connections Board to facilitate this and a channel in our Discord server.
We do run a quarterly 101 to get you up to speed with the basics and occasionally do one-off teaching events if there is someone who has an idea and a skill they want to share more formally.



Probably! Feel free to offer any skill share in our opening circle (just grab a rainbow lanyarded volunteer and let us know and we’ll let folks know), via our Connections Board or if you’d like to present a more formal class send us a DM on fet, DM one of the logistics team in our Discord or chat to a rainbow lanyarded volunteer about it in person.



When we say we are not a play event the things we infer by that statement are:

the lights are brighter, music is more background level volume to allow for low level talking
this is an environment to expect people to chat, teach each other, work in small groups, or practicing tying 1-to-1, labing (practicing) techniques
this is an environment where vanilla clothing is required
this is an environment where being in a severely altered headspace is not appropriate
this an environment where aftercare space is not provided
there are no DM’s monitoring peoples safety during their tying
this is a rope specific space, other things such as impact which may be sometimes be included in rope play, are not allowed in the space




What to expect from each type of event is available in the event descriptions. On a basic level expect more chatting and groups working on self tying or learning skills together at Peer Share events and at Open Tying expect most socialising to happen in the kitchen area while people are more likely to be tying together in a more scene-adjacent way.

title: Ropes in Space
text:
Ropes in Space is a rope event run every secon Monday in Glasgow. It is a peer-learning event, meaning we have no formal teaching or authority at the event. However, there will always be someone on hand to make sure you feel welcome. They are also present to answer questions and take feedback.
We aim to be a relaxed environment in which you can practice rope: alone, partnered, as a rigger, bottom, switch – however you want to explore rope!

title: Ropes in Space
text:
The event
The event is held in Glasgow, close to public transport links to the city centre. Precise location is disclosed to attendees. We start at 6:30pm, and the event ends at 10:30pm.
While anyone is welcome to any session if you are brand new to rope or need a refresher our total beginner 101s for 2026 will run on:

26th of January
20th of April
27th of July
19th of October

Aside from quarterly 101s we have two different types of sessions: Peer Share and Open Tying.
The first event each month will be a Peer Share session which means you can expect a learning focused atmosphere perfect to bring skills you want to practice, questions you have, or things you want to geek out about and share. Music will be at a lower level to allow for conversations. This will not be a traditional class/formal rope education format.
Unless otherwise advertised the second event each month will be an Open Tying session. Which means you can expect to find more vibes and less chat to facilitate space to really get into tying. Music will be at a slightly increased volume and attendees will be reminded to keep chat to a minimum.
Please note that participation in any of the aspects outlined above is entirely optional, and you may use the space for free-tying as you see fit!

title: Ropes in Space
text:
Transparency & Feedback
Should you need to report feedback on the event anonymously, you can do via this form. Responses to the feedback form are monitored by volunteers in RiS’ logistics and safety teams.

title: Ropes in Space
text:
Contact
If you have any queries about the event, or feedback you would like to provide, please message the Fetlife page and a member of the team will get back to you!

title: Anchor Point
text:
A full weekend of rope education, play and performance hosted by Ropes in Space. Aiming to break down geographical barriers to rope education in Scotland by bringing exciting teachers from further afield whilst also platforming local and up and coming teachers.
Ropes in Space is a community led organisation running peer learning events and rope jams in Glasgow.

title: Anchor Point
text:
Schedule

Friday 7pm - 10pm: Intros and icebreakers. A chance to get comfortable in the space and get to know the other attendees in an informal environment. We will also run a “Speed Roping” (Like speed dating!) session to help break the ice.
Saturday 10am - 6pm: Workshops
Saturday 7pm - 11pm: Rope Jam and Performances
Sunday 10am - 5pm: Workshops

We will be running two classes concurrently throughout the event so you are not guaranteed participation in all of your preferred classes. We will send out registration forms to all ticket holders in due course and our full class schedule will be arranged to try to accommodate as many people’s first choices as we possibly can.

title: Anchor Point
text:
Class List

Cad and Evitrii (aka Bast): Freeform Suspension*, Rope Dance.
Quartz and PeachyRopes: Shame, Objectification and Humiliation, Rope for Gender Euphoria*
Brig and Belial: Wrestling with Rope
Ginger and Farah: Embodied Tying
Lola: Predicaments and Pain
Mindorra: Hangers and Uplines and Locks, Oh My! *
Setonix: Tying Decorative Corsets

*These classes will have requirements for entry.

title: Anchor Point
text:
Requirements For Attendance
While we don’t want to gatekeep attendance to Anchor point we do not recommend our event for absolute beginners to rope.
A few classes will have some clearly communicated skill requirements for safety reasons and the majority of classes will assume basic competence with rope handling, understanding of basic safety and the ability to tie a few beginner level frictions and columns.
For those intending to solely attend as a rope bottom, some experience in rope and competency in communicating both your needs in rope and also knowledge on basic risk awareness such as the difference between circulation and nerve issues, is expected in order to facilitate good learning experiences and ensure safety for all.
If you are not sure about if you meet any of the requirements to attend feel free to reach out via message or discuss it with us at one of our peer rope events. There is still plenty of time to build these skills and we will be focusing on these competencies in our 101 and 102 sessions at our fortnightly rope gatherings in the lead up to the event.
If you do choose to join us as a beginner and find yourself out of your depth we ask that you are prepared to sit back and follow as much as you can rather than divert the teachers or other participants to assist you during the class.

title: Anchor Point
text:
Ticket Info and Financial Transparency
Tickets are issued individually as we reconise that not everyone wants to attend events in a fixed tying partnership. Confident self-tyers are welcome to attend solo although not all of our classes will be easily adaptable for solo tying. Tying partnerships (up to 3 people) for each class should be arranged prior to registration opening as we will need this information to allocate classes.
We want to make this event as financially transparent and accessible as possible so we have decided to share our number crunching and let you pick your price - with a standard price of £150 for the whole weekend of workshops, Friday speed roping and Saturday Rope Jam and Performances. We are also offering payment plans of either 3 or 4 equal payments to increase access for those on lower incomes. Our teachers have kindly agreed a profit share model with us and our organisers are all working on a voluntary basis to enable us to offer this flexibility to you. If none of our standard prices are accessible to you or you need smaller installments to pay full price please apply for a solidarity ticket here and we will get back to you with an offer toward the end of the ticket sales period.

If ticket sales average £125: our teachers get a basic wage and RiS could add to our library or buy one or two comfier mats for tying on.
If ticket sales average £150: our teachers get standard rope educator fee and RiS could add to our library or upgrade the majority of our mats.
If ticket sales average £175: we’re able to offer solidarity tickets to more people, our teachers get a higher level rope educator wage and RiS could get a second suspension frame.

title: Anchor Point
section: Airborne Disease Mitigation and Illness Policy
text:
Airborne Disease Mitigation and Illness Policy
We recognise COVID-19 and other increasingly occurring pathogens are an ongoing risk to all and are especially impactful to disabled, chronically ill, and immuno-compromised people’s right to participate in public life and recreation. We will be taking steps to risk mitgation on this front and we ask all attendees to read and agree to our policy which can be seen in full on our Fetlife page.

title: Anchor Point
section: Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy
text:
Code of Conduct and Safeguarding Policy
Our full Code of Conduct is published on Fetlife. We expect all attendees to familiarise themselves with, and abide by, our Code of Conduct for the duration of the event. We ask that a Fetlife or other kinky social media handle be included with all ticket purchases to allow us to properly vet all attendees. Our full Safeguarding Policy is available to read on Fetlife. We reserve the right to reject and refund a ticket purchase at the discretion of the organisers.

title: Anchor Point
text:
Refund Policy
Full refunds, less processing fees, will be available via your Ticket Tailor account until the 4th of July at 6pm, when ticket sales will close. Any further refunds will be at the discretion of organisers.

title: Code of Conduct
text:
Code of Conduct

We are a rope-focused community group. Our main focus is hosting a regular peer learning event – this is not a play party unless explicitly stated otherwise.
Our events run on the premise of equality and respect and to this aim we reject racism, homophobia, sexism, transphobia, breaches of consent, body shaming, ableism and classism, in all forms whether they are blatant or come in the form of microaggressions.
Please do not assume anyone’s gender or pronouns.
Do not touch another person, their rope or belongings without specific consent.
Please do not take photographs without the consent of everyone who would be in the image (including those in the background).
No full nudity or fetish wear, think comfy gym/dance gear.
We practice explicit, informed and embodied or enthusiastic consent (the spirit of this statement is more important than the specific vocabulary chosen to describe it). If you are unsure if consent has been given, seek clarification before proceeding.
The event safeword is Red. If this safeword is used and you do not move to end your tying, someone may intervene to make sure the safeword is being respected and acted upon.
We follow R.A.C.K (Risk Aware Consensual Kink) and believe nothing is inherently safe or without risk. With this in mind, please take responsibility for your own safety and those you are tying with. Have your own safety shears/equipment checked and to hand. We have no DM’s, ask a community member to be a spotter if required and clearly specify what you need from them if you do so. Be upfront in negotiations regarding any health and safety issues relating to your tying.
Respect other peoples’ scenes. Although we are a learning space please do not interrupt to ask questions or give suggestions unless you have negotiated permission or there are immediate safety concerns, maintain a respectful distance and ask before actively spectating. This applies for partnered and self-tying.
Our environment is a relaxed one, and socialising is part of what makes us a community, but please be mindful of volume levels near others tying.
This event is a sober event. Please do not arrive in an altered state or consume substances such as alcohol or drugs at the event.
If you have any concerns or questions, there are allocated ‘feedback people’ (identified by wearing lanyards) at each event who you can feel free to approach. If you prefer you can contact the Fetlife page or use our anonymous feedback form
